sections.h2: What a Madison Heights homeowner should know before selling
sections.html:
Three local points shape a Madison Heights sale: the city sends its own property tax bills, it licenses landlords but skips resale inspections, and the transfer affidavit goes to an office on Thirteen Mile Road. Once those are handled, the closing follows the usual Michigan steps.

The 2025 estimate of 28,297 people sits 0.6% under the 2020 base. Owners occupy 64.8% of the homes, valued at a median of $199,100 for 2020 to 2024, while renters pay a median gross rent of $1,176. Median household income is $69,503.

Madison Heights is a compact Oakland County city about 12 miles north of downtown Detroit. Troy, Royal Oak, Hazel Park and Warren ring the city, and its eastern edge at Dequindre Road doubles as the line between Oakland and Macomb counties. I-75 skirts the west side while I-696 marks much of the south. About 91% of its buildings are single-family homes or condominiums, roughly 9,800 owners, yet light industrial and commercial property supplies around 60% of the tax base.

Madison District Public Schools and Lamphere Public Schools serve different addresses, so confirm which one covers your street before you describe the school zone.

sections.h2: Will Madison Heights make me pass an inspection to sell?
sections.html:
No. City staff state that Madison Heights neither requires nor provides resale inspections, so you can list or sign a purchase agreement without booking a walk-through.

Rentals are a separate matter. An owner who lets someone else live in a Madison Heights house needs a landlord license, even when no rent is charged. A qualified relative living there waives both the fee and the inspection. Without a license, an owner cannot collect rent or evict, a point worth settling before a tenant-occupied house goes on the market.

Property typeFee, new or renewal
Single-family home$210

The first license may run under three years with a prorated fee, and each renewal covers four years and brings a fresh inspection. The city will not issue a license while property taxes, special assessments or water bills are unpaid.

The city's treasury handles both bills directly. Early July brings the summer bill, payable through August 31 with no penalty, and early December brings the winter bill, payable through February 17.

After August 31, a 4% penalty applies from September 1, and a further 1/2% accrues each month. Winter bills pick up a 3% penalty on February 18. City Hall stops taking payment after March 2, and from March 3 the Oakland County Treasurer collects, with extra penalties added. A drop box outside City Hall takes checks and money orders around the clock.

A sale reopens the next owner's number. In the year after a transfer, taxable value jumps to the state equalized value under MCL 211.27a, so a long-held house that has been capped for decades can produce a much larger bill for the buyer. If you took the principal residence exemption, file a rescission after you move out. MCL 211.7cc sets a 90-day window and charges $5 a day, to a maximum of $200, for lateness. Closing agents must give both sides the affidavit and rescission forms at the table.

sections.h2: Which documents and fees come with a Madison Heights closing?
sections.html:
A typical closing here involves a recorded deed, a tax certification if the deed carries a warranty, transfer tax and the city affidavit. A title company usually takes care of the deed work and the certificate.

  • Recording: Oakland County's Register of Deeds examines each document before recording it. The page needs a 2.5 inch margin at the top and a notary's signature.
  • Tax certification: taxes must show as current on a warranty deed, and the county charges $5.
  • Transfer tax: state and county tax together run $4.30 per $500 of price. Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt under MCL 207.526.
  • City affidavit: file it with the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road within 45 days. A late residential filing costs $5 a day up to $200, and commercial or industrial property costs $25 a day up to $1,000.

Ask the Oakland County Register of Deeds for the current recording fee before mailing anything. Its Sheriff Deed and Clerk Deed redemption desk is a separate service and does not affect an ordinary sale.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Madison Heights house?
sections.html:
Pick by how much time you have and what shape the house is in. Compare each route by the money left after repairs, carrying costs and closing fees, since a high list price can shrink quickly.

  • Agent listing: showings and wide exposure, with the buyer's lender and appraisal setting the timeline.
  • For sale by owner: full control of price and terms, and the disclosures and paperwork fall on you.
  • Cash purchase: no lender step, and the buyer takes the house with its repairs or a tenant already inside.

If a cash sale appeals, tell us the Madison Heights address and what shape the place is in, and we will price it as it stands.

Pull your latest tax bills and confirm both are paid or ready to be prorated, since City Hall stops taking payment after March 2 and the county takes over from there. If the house was rented, confirm the landlord license status, because the city will not issue one while taxes, special assessments or water bills are unpaid. Ask your title company to bring the affidavit and rescission forms to the table. After closing, send the transfer affidavit to the Assessing Department on time and file your own rescission within the 90-day window. A cash buyer can take over these steps with you, and because there is no lender, the buyer can usually close on the date you choose.

The paperwork has a rhythm. Before the sale, you deal with taxes and any landlord license. At the table, the title company handles the deed, the certificate and the transfer tax. Within 45 days, the buyer files the affidavit with the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road. Within 90 days, you cancel the exemption on the house you left. If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease before you promise a possession date, and ask the buyer in writing whether the tenant will stay.

faqs.q: Does Madison Heights inspect houses at resale?
faqs.a: No. The city does not require or provide resale inspections. Inspections come up only with landlord licensing, and an owner-occupied sale does not trigger one.

faqs.q: Can a tenant stay in the house while I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the house carries a city landlord license. The license is mandatory for any occupied home the owner does not live in, though a qualified relative waives the fee and inspection. Without it, rent collection and eviction are off the table.

faqs.q: What transfer tax does a Madison Heights seller owe?
faqs.a: State and county tax together come to $4.30 per $500 of price. The deed has to show the value or carry an affidavit stating it.

faqs.q: Where do I send Madison Heights taxes after March 2?
faqs.a: To the Oakland County Treasurer. City Hall accepts payment only through March 2, and the county adds penalties after that.

faqs.q: What happens if I file the transfer affidavit late?
faqs.a: The city fines $5 per day up to $200 for a residential property. The deadline is 45 days after the transfer, and the form goes to the Assessing Department.
